pr_title: Make `range` and `generate_series` table in-out functions, and fix several issues with table in-out functions
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/5762
Fixes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/6917
Fixes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/7846
Fixes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/10927
Fixes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/11393


This PR moves the `range` and `generate_series` from the standard table function API to the table in-out function API. As a result, these functions can be used in lateral joins and subqueries and are no longer limited to taking only literal parameters. For example:

```sql
D select * from (select 5 AS a), range(a);
┌───────┬───────┐
│   a   │ range │
│ int32 │ int64 │
├───────┼───────┤
│     5 │     0 │
│     5 │     1 │
│     5 │     2 │
│     5 │     3 │
│     5 │     4 │
└───────┴───────┘
-- or
D select (select count(*) from range(a)) AS result from (select 5 AS a);
┌────────┐
│ result │
│ int64  │
├────────┤
│      5 │
└────────┘
-- or even
D select * from range(5) t(a), range(a) t2(b) order by all;
┌───────┬───────┐
│   a   │   b   │
│ int64 │ int64 │
├───────┼───────┤
│     1 │     0 │
│     2 │     0 │
│     2 │     1 │
│     3 │     0 │
│     3 │     1 │
│     3 │     2 │
│     4 │     0 │
│     4 │     1 │
│     4 │     2 │
│     4 │     3 │
├───────┴───────┤
│    10 rows    │
└───────────────┘
```

#### Table In-Out Function Fixes

This PR also fixes several issues with table in-out functions. Previously, table in-out functions could only have a `TABLE` parameter, which meant they did not support function overloads. In addition, they would behave in an unusual way when dealing with scalar subqueries, where they would instead of treating them like a scalar subquery move the subquery into the main query plan, e.g.:

```sql
D SELECT * FROM UNNEST((SELECT ARRAY[1,2,3] UNION ALL SELECT ARRAY[4,5])) t(result);
┌────────┐
│ result │
│ int32  │
├────────┤
│      1 │
│      2 │
│      3 │
│      4 │
│      5 │
└────────┘
```

This PR maintains this behavior for functions that have `TABLE` parameters for backwards compatibility, but now allows table in-out functions to be created with any parameters. When created with regular parameters, they will behave identically to other SQL functions where scalar subqueries will be treated like regular scalar subqueries instead of having special treatment, including having casts inserted by the system where required.


#### Backwards compatibility

For backwards compatibility, and for more readable query plans, the table in-out functions are now executed as regular table functions when the parameters are constant. This keeps query plans the same and as readable as before when using constant parameters, e.g.:

```sql
D explain from range(100);
┌───────────────────────────┐
│           RANGE           │
│   ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─   │
│          EC: 100          │
└───────────────────────────┘  

```

In-out function nodes are only created when required (by e.g. using the function in a lateral join).

This also keeps the serialization of plans backwards compatible for these functions. The serialization tests have also been updated to test this. 


#### Correlated Subqueries

This PR also fixes a number of issues with table in-out functions and correlated subqueries. While the above "flattening" technique made single-level scalar subqueries work, e.g.:

```sql
D select * from (select [1,2,3] a), unnest((select a));
┌───────────┬───────┐
│     a     │   a   │
│  int32[]  │ int32 │
├───────────┼───────┤
│ [1, 2, 3] │     1 │
│ [1, 2, 3] │     2 │
│ [1, 2, 3] │     3 │
└───────────┴───────┘
```

There were problems with multi-layered scalar subqueries as the unflattening was not done correctly at all levels:


```sql
D select * from (select [1,2,3] a), unnest((select (select a)));
-- INTERNAL Error: Expression with depth > 1 detected in non-lateral join
```

This PR fixes these issues by correctly expanding subqueries within the children of table in-out functions.


#### Unnest Output Name

The `unnest` function would previously copy the output of its column from the input, e.g.:


```sql
D select * from unnest(array[1,2,3]);
┌──────────────────┐
│ (ARRAY[1, 2, 3]) │
│      int32       │
├──────────────────┤
│                1 │
│                2 │
│                3 │
└──────────────────┘
```

This is even more confusing when using lateral joins:

```sql
select * from (select array[1,2,3] l), unnest(l);
┌───────────┬───────┐
│     l     │   l   │
│  int32[]  │ int32 │
├───────────┼───────┤
│ [1, 2, 3] │     1 │
│ [1, 2, 3] │     2 │
│ [1, 2, 3] │     3 │
└───────────┴───────┘
```

This is rather confusing and not very useful. This PR changes the naming to match Postgres, where the column name is always `unnest` instead if no alias is provided.

```sql
select * from unnest(array[1,2,3]);
┌────────┐
│ unnest │
│ int32  │
├────────┤
│      1 │
│      2 │
│      3 │
└────────┘
```

While this is technically a breaking change - the old behavior is quite hostile, so I don't think it will break anyone's scripts (but will likely be proven wrong :)).

issue_context.title: `range`/`generate_series` misinterpret types of correlated columns
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

When using `range` or `generate_series` in a correlated position—i.e., their arguments access columns/rows to the left in the same `FROM`-clause—they seem to misinterpret the types of said variables as `varchar`s.

### To Reproduce

```sql
SELECT x FROM (SELECT 32 AS a) AS _, LATERAL range(a) AS __(x);
```

### OS:

mac OS (aarch64)

### DuckDB Version:

dev (cef3bdc)

### DuckDB Client:

cli

### Full Name:

Tim Fischer

### Affiliation:

Database Research Group Tübingen

### Have you tried this on the latest `master` branch?

- [X] I agree

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [X] I agree
comments:
Thanks for the report!

This is the same issue as #5762, and occurs because `range` is not implemented as a table-in-out function. Work is in progress to fix that, but currently `range` is not supported as a lateral function.
Thanks for the quick response! It seems my GitHub-Fu is not as good as I thought! I'll close this issue then. 👋

Do we want to throw an InternalException here?
This could happen if an extension registers a new overload for a function
I think it's fine to throw an internal exception if an extension screws up - if we had to guard against internal exceptions from extensions that would complicate system design quite a bit :)
